A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ConDU research, with matching method definitions and benchmark results. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ConDU experiments on MTIL, few-shot MTIL and task-agnostic MTIL, alongside sensitivity, task-order and representation analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds TinyImageNet results, component ablations, hardware comparisons, timing measurements and sessionwise accuracy results.

M1.justification: v1 Section 2 and v3 Section 4 retain independent task fine-tuning, sign-based maximum-magnitude fusion, binary masks, rescaling, expert reconstruction, pretrained-model prototypes and top-K logit aggregation. Renaming task-specific models as task experts and evaluating TinyImageNet do not document a procedural change.

E1.justification: The original eleven-dataset MTIL suite and its variants remain. v3 Appendix D adds TinyImageNet class-incremental learning, extending evaluation to a new dataset and an expanding class space with task-agnostic prediction.

E2.justification: v3 Figure 4 adds comparisons with LoRA variants of LwF, LwF-VR and WiSE-FT, while Table 12 adds Individual FT with LoRA. The original benchmark comparator sets remain in the full tables: Dual-RAIL disappears from the main few-shot display but remains evaluated in Appendix Table 8.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a TinyImageNet protocol with 100 initial classes followed by ten 10-class or twenty 5-class increments and final task-agnostic accuracy, plus hardware and timing comparison procedures. Section 5.1 also changes the reported Average metric from accuracy over seen tasks to averaging across all sessions, including before a task is encountered. Appendix A retains the earlier definition, so the PDFs do not establish that the unchanged MTIL scores were recomputed.

E4.justification: v3 adds direct tests of pretrained versus expert feature matching, removal of rescalers, and inference with the unified model alone. It also adds hardware robustness, parameter-accuracy and runtime comparisons, an integrated Individual FT comparison, and sessionwise forgetting analysis. The original K sensitivity and alternative task-order analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, standard deviations or significance tests. The added experiments do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The matched full MTIL, few-shot, task-agnostic and alternative-order tables retain their scores apart from rounding. v3 adds substantial results, including TinyImageNet ConDU FT accuracies of 71.74% and 71.49% for the two incremental settings, component ablations, hardware comparisons and timing measurements. The K sweep also changes its reported optimum from 70.33% at K=4 in v1 Table 3 to 70.8% at K=5 in v3 Table 11.

T1.justification: v1 Appendix G claims negligible effects from arriving models and vanishing average update magnitudes. v3 replaces this continual-arrival argument with Theorem 1 concerning asymptotic expected nonincrease of individual update magnitudes, adding boundedness and common-sign assumptions. Its rewritten proof adds an order-statistic lemma and changes the fixed-model corollary, while retaining much of the earlier fixed-model convergence argument.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central contributions: ConDU model fusion and reconstruction, compatibility with full and parameter-efficient fine-tuning, zero-shot prediction aggregation, and an up-to-2% average-performance advantage. The stronger novelty wording and added supporting analyses do not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations linking pretrained features to shared representations and rescalers to magnitude preservation, and clarifies the unified model's storage role. It adds guidance on FT versus LoRA, parallel-inference resource requirements, accuracy-storage tradeoffs and forgetting after MNIST. Its few-shot interpretation also changes from second-best Last performance to superiority, despite retaining the stronger Dual-RAIL result in Table 8.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-access link, a reproducibility statement, computing-platform information, phase-level runtime measurements and details of the t-SNE embedding procedure. The previously documented backbone, optimizer, batch size, MTIL training budgets and LoRA storage configuration remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion largely moves from v1 Appendix D to v3 Section 2. Limited citation changes add Zenke et al.'s synaptic intelligence work and remove the Liu et al. prompting survey, Wang et al. continual-learning survey and Zhao et al. SAFE paper. v3 also more explicitly contrasts ConDU with direct iterative model merging.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes the narrative, moving related work, problem formulation and experimental settings into the main text, expanding discussion and removing the standalone conclusion. It condenses the introductory method walkthrough, consistently adopts task-expert terminology, reorganizes the appendices and adds reproducibility, ethics and LLM-use statements.

P2.justification: The framework and fusion diagrams are extensively redrawn, and inference and prototype illustrations are redistributed. The t-SNE display gains separate comparisons, legends and magnified regions; a parameter-accuracy plot and several analysis tables are added. Retained benchmark tables are relocated and restyled with highlighted ConDU rows, and the main few-shot display omits a comparator still present in the appendix.

improvement.justification: New component ablations, class-incremental tests and resource analyses strengthen diagnostic evidence. However, v1's second-best few-shot Last result becomes a superiority claim despite v3 retaining Dual-RAIL's 77.9% versus ConDU's 77.4%; Section 6's 62% timing saving conflicts with approximately 52% in Appendix I. The revised proof also unjustifiably equates an expectation of a ratio with a ratio of expectations in Equation 3. These empirical benefits and problems in the reliability of the claims leave the net quality direction uncertain.
